name: Agamand Family Sword
summary: In northern Tirisfal, the Agamand Family Sword remains in the family crypt. The tarnished blade once marked the wealth and standing of the mill-owning dynasty, and Coleman Farthing now seeks it to erase their legacy.

sections.title: A Legacy in the Tomb
sections.body: The Agamands once held great wealth and influence through their mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, the family met a gruesome end, and their bodies rose as mindless thralls of the Lich King. Their ancestral weapons, including the ceremonial sword, were sealed inside the Agamand Family Crypt at the northern edge of the mills. Taking these blades from their burial racks is an act meant to break the memory and noble standing of the fallen household.

sections.title: Vengeance from Beyond the Grave
sections.body: Coleman Farthing, a Forsaken living in Brill, seeks the sword. He served the Agamands in life and blames his former masters for his death. Farthing sends adventurers to claim the sword along with the dynasty's ancestral axe, dagger, and mace. He aims to strip the shambling Agamands of their last shred of honor and extinguish their bloodline's dignity.

faq.q: What is the Agamand Family Sword?
faq.answer: The Agamand Family Sword is an ancestral weapon of the Agamands, a prominent noble family that ran the grain mills in northern Tirisfal Glades before Lordaeron fell.

The sword rests on a weapon rack inside the Agamand Family Crypt, at the northern edge of Agamand Mills in Tirisfal Glades. Scourge thralls and risen members of the Agamand bloodline defend the crypt.

faq.q: Why does Coleman Farthing want this sword?
faq.answer: Coleman Farthing served the Agamand family in life and blames them for his death. He seeks their heirloom weapons to strip away their remaining honor and erase the memory of their dynasty.

faq.q: What happened to the Agamand family?
faq.answer: The Agamands were slaughtered during the Scourge invasion of Lordaeron. Their dead remain trapped in mindless service to the Lich King, haunting their ancestral estate and crypt.

angles.text: For the Forsaken, reclaiming artifacts from Tirisfal's former nobility means settling scores with a living past that failed to protect them.
As a warrior, you see a blade once polished as an emblem of Lordaeron's aristocracy, now neglected in an unhallowed tomb and marked by ruined martial pride.
